hook.en: A sustained joint glide applied by the therapist while the patient performs the movement that normally hurts, aiming for an instant pain-free result.
hook.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) mein therapist ek sustained accessory glide deta hai aur patient usi waqt apni active movement karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: Mobilization With Movement (MWM) combines a gentle sustained glide with the patient's own active movement. You search for a glide direction that makes the previously painful movement easy and pain-free right now. If it works, you repeat it; if it does not, you stop.
text.ur: MWM passive accessory glide aur patient ki active movement ko combine karta hai. Therapist glide ki direction, angle ya assistance ko adjust karta hai; patient apni movement khud karta hai. Is liye yeh sirf therapist ke hand se joint move karna nahi, balkay movement ke response ko foran observe karna bhi hai.

simpler.en: A sustained joint glide applied by the therapist while the patient performs the movement that normally hurts, aiming for an instant pain-free result.
simpler.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) mein therapist ek sustained accessory glide deta hai aur patient usi waqt apni active movement karta hai.

text.en: It is like adjusting a sticky drawer while the person pulls it open. You try a small nudge in different directions until the drawer slides freely, instead of forcing it.
text.ur: Yeh atke hue darazon ko theek karne jaisa hai jab koi usay khol raha ho. Aap mukhtalif directions mein halka sa dhakka try karte hain jab tak daraz aaram se na khul jaye — zabardasti nahi karte.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** The patient must be able to do the movement without pain while you apply the glide. No instant improvement means the glide is wrong; do not persist.
**2.** Hold the glide the whole time the patient moves, then repeat several times and finish with gentle overpressure only if painless.
**3.** The result should carry over: the movement stays better after you release (the 'long-lasting' rule).
text.ur: Pehle woh active movement identify karein jo dard, stiffness ya function ki limitation ko reproduce karti hai. Mulligan Mobilization with Movement mein therapist accessory glide deta hai jab patient active movement karta hai. Glide ke saath movement comfortable honi chahiye; pain barhe to zabardasti continue na karein.

question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **PILL response** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en: Pain-free, Instant result, Long-lasting. The three signs that an MWM is right.

text.en:
So when does **Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)** make sense?
• A clearly painful or restricted movement that is easy to repeat, for example painful gripping at the elbow or restricted ankle dorsiflexion.
• Joints that can be glided safely in a direction that changes the movement at once.
text.ur:
To **Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)** kab samajh mein aati hai?
• A clearly painful or restricted movement that is easy to repeat, for example painful gripping at the elbow or restricted ankle dorsiflexion.
• Joints that can be glided safely in a direction that changes the movement at once.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• No immediate pain-free improvement after a few careful tries.
• Unstable joints, fractures, infection or inflammation, and where glides are unsafe.
• Any increase in pain, dizziness or neurological symptoms.
text.ur: Acute highly irritable condition, postoperative restrictions ya uncertain joint stability mein pehle clinical screening aur relevant precautions zaroor dekhein. Fracture ya instability ka shak, serious neurological/vascular warning signs, ya aisa dard jo modification se acceptable na ho, mein technique jari na rakhein. Improvement ko exercise aur functional practice ke sath integrate karna aksar zaroori hota hai.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Find the painful movement
steps.detail: Example: pain when gripping with the elbow extended in tennis elbow. Record the pain score.

steps.title: Search for the glide
steps.detail: Try a gentle glide (for example, sideways at the elbow) and ask the patient to repeat the movement.

steps.title: Check the PILL
steps.detail: The movement should become pain-free right now. If not, adjust the direction slightly, or abandon the technique.

steps.title: Hold and repeat
steps.detail: Hold the glide while the patient performs the movement 6-10 times.

steps.title: Add gentle overpressure only if painless
Release and retest
steps.detail: Check if the improvement stays. Teach a home version if suitable.

beats.ur: Pehle patient ki ek relevant painful ya restricted movement ko baseline ke taur par note karein. Phir suitable accessory glide ke sath movement repeat karwayein. Force, direction aur position ko response ke mutabiq adjust karein. Overpressure sirf tab consider karein jab clinically munasib ho aur movement acceptable rahe. Aakhir mein glide ke baghair movement dobara check karein.

question.en: Imagine the patient is in front of you. What do you do FIRST?
question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: about 6-10 repetitions, 2-3 sets, only if the movement is pain-free. Repeat for sessions if the benefit persists; if it fades quickly, rethink.
text.ur:
Kitna? Dose ki teaching range:
Typical teaching range: about 6-10 repetitions, 2-3 sets, only if the movement is pain-free. Repeat for sessions if the benefit persists; if it fades quickly, rethink.

beats.patient: Sana, 38, hairdresser, outer elbow pain when gripping her hairdryer.
beats.assessment: Painful grip: 7/10. Pain-free grip is very weak.
beats.treatment: You apply a gentle sideways glide of the forearm at the elbow while she grips. Pain falls to 1/10 during the grip. She repeats 10 times, 3 sets.
beats.reassess: After release the grip is pain-free at 2/10 and stronger. You add strengthening exercises and review. Had the pain stayed at 7/10 you would have changed the glide or stopped.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein ek patient ko ankle dorsiflexion ke waqt discomfort aur restriction hai. Assessment ke baad therapist ek gentle glide ke sath patient se knee-forward movement karwata hai. Agar movement comfortable aur behtar ho, to therapist glide hatakar dobara test karta hai. Yeh fictional example hai, kisi specific ankle condition ke liye guaranteed result ya prescription nahi.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Continuing when pain does not drop instantly.
• Applying the glide with so much force it hurts.
• Giving no follow-up exercise so the improvement fades.
text.ur: Pain ke bawajood movement repeat karna ya sirf session mein behtar feel hone ko success samajhna aam ghalti hai. Range, pain aur relevant function ko pehle aur baad mein same tareeqe se compare karein. Agar behtari na ho to setup reassess karein; force bas barhana jawab nahi.

text.en: Small trials and reviews suggest short-term benefit for conditions such as tennis elbow and ankle stiffness, but the evidence quality varies. The mechanism is unclear and may include pain modulation.
text.ur: Mulligan approach har musculoskeletal condition ka universal solution nahi. Response patient aur selected movement ke mutabiq vary kar sakta hai. Isay active rehabilitation aur broader management ke context mein dekhein, aur English chapter ki evidence limitations ko barqarar rakhein.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Glide, move, ask: if it is not pain-free and instant, it is not the right glide.**
